title: Modeling a Real-World Quantity with a Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Outline the steps for modeling a real-world quantity with a function, then demonstrate them on a rectangle with fixed perimeter 40 whose area depends on its width.
finalAnswer: Steps: identify variables, choose the domain, express the rule, then validate against data. For the rectangle: $A(w) = w(20 - w)$ with natural modeling domain $0 < w < 20$.

steps.title: Identify the Variables
steps.explanation: Decide which quantity varies freely (the independent variable) and which one you want to predict (the dependent variable). Naming and units matter: width in meters, area in square meters.
steps.why: Every model begins by separating the input you control from the output you want.

steps.title: Choose a Realistic Domain
steps.explanation: The physical constraints shrink the natural algebraic domain: widths at or beyond 20 force a nonpositive length, which describes no rectangle. Modeling domains are chosen by the situation, not only by the formula.
steps.why: A formula without its meaningful domain answers the wrong question.

steps.title: Express the Rule
steps.explanation: Combine the geometric relations into one formula for the dependent variable in terms of the independent one. Here the perimeter constraint eliminates the length, leaving the quadratic area model A(w) = 20w - w^2.
steps.why: Reducing everything to a single-variable rule is what makes the function usable for optimization later.

steps.title: Validate with Data and Interpret
steps.explanation: Test endpoints of Reason: the 10 by 10 square should give the largest area, and swapping width with length should not change the area, which the symmetry A(5) = A(15) reflects. Compare predictions with measured examples before trusting the model.
steps.why: Validation separates a plausible model from a decorative formula.
